title: Inspections of HDB Buildings for Structural Integrity and Design
what_it_is: Inspections of HDB Buildings for Structural Integrity and Design

sections.label: Periodic structural inspection requirements
sections.summary: Building owners must engage PEs for PSI every 10 years for residential buildings and every five years for other types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Building owners have to engage PEs to conduct the PSI every 10 years for residential buildings and every five years for other building types.

sections.label: HDB structural and facade inspections
sections.summary: HDB will conduct more stringent structural integrity inspections and audit external facade inspections on its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: HDB will step in on its own to do more stringent inspections and checks of structural integrity and also audit inspections of external building facades.

sections.label: HDB facade repair co-payment
sections.summary: HDB will pay 50% of Town Councils' repair costs for external facade finishes of HDB buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under this co-payment scheme, HDB will pay 50% of the repair cost incurred by Town Councils to repair external facade finishes of HDB buildings.

sections.label: HDB extra checks on older blocks
sections.summary: HDB will do five-year checks on older blocks on top of Town Council work and selective annual facade inspections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But HDB, being a good developer, will do its own checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, for older blocks, HDB will do five-year checks on top of what the Town Council is supposed to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And HDB will also selectively do annual inspections for the older blocks for building facades.

sections.label: Investigation of dislodged structure and insurance
sections.summary: PEs investigating are checking the impacted building and prioritising similar buildings by the same contractor for safety.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: And considering that the dislodged structure could weigh up to one tonne, are there insurance policies in place for public liability, hospitalisation and other compensation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would just say that in the investigation that is ongoing by the PEs, they are looking not only at the impacted building but they have also given priority to checking on similar buildings of similar design done by the same contractor to make sure that these are safe.

sections.label: Risk-based inspection and co-payment
sections.summary: HDB will assess building materials and conditions rather than a specific year, focusing more on older blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: HDB will look at risks and  materials in that particular building, how they were used, and the materials have changed over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the past, we did not use precast concrete, now we do and, so, if you look at older blocks, generally, say, those built in the 1980s, 1970s, certainly, the materials used then, not just by HDB, by any developer then, are very different from the materials used today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, rather than have a specific year and say everything before that qualifies, everything after that does not qualify, we will look at the building materials and the conditions and, naturally, we would give greater focus to the older blocks, as I think all Town Councils should, within their own risk-based assessment and inspection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On payments, I understand that Town Councils would certainly like to have higher co-payments from HDB, particularly if you have a greater proportion of older blocks.
